title: Dutch Elm: Ancient Dutch Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: Survivors of the disease that carries their own name: Amsterdam's tallest tree, a Hague elm from the 1830s, and a Portland elm saved by a parked car.
intro: Dutch elm disease is named for the country that first identified it, which makes every mapped tree of this hybrid a small act of defiance. Amsterdam's Oudemanhuispoort elm has turned a brick-walled courtyard into an advantage, reaching 35 metres because the only direction open to it was up, and a second Amsterdam elm is the last of roughly thirty planted outside Centraal station in 1889, the rest lost to the epidemic decades ago. The Hague's Malieveld elm dates to the 1830s and has now outlived two separate waves of the disease, the second and worse one arriving in the 1970s. In Portland, the Rockey elm survived a 1963 demolition order only because an architect parked his car where the removal crew needed to stand. Each of these is a tree the fungus could have taken and did not.
